case_title.reason: Matches the judgment's caption, Prakash v. State of Karnataka.

number_of_accused.reason: Single appellant, Prakash, whose conviction is decided.

accused_gender.reason: The accused is referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is stated.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is stated.

accused_occupation.reason: Only residence in Nagenahalli village is mentioned; no occupation is stated.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth or class appears.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: The victim, Gangamma, is referred to as female.

victim_age.reason: The victim's age is not stated.

victim_caste.reason: No caste of the victim is stated.

victim_religion.reason: No religion of the victim is stated.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment states the deceased did not know who the appellant was, so he was a stranger.

offence_category.reason: The main charge is murder under s.302.

statutory_provisions.reason: s.302 is shown in the header; theft section is not given, as the value notes.

weapon.reason: The steel rod used to kill the deceased is identified as the weapon.

evidence_type.correct_value: Circumstantial: witness identification of presence at house, fingerprint on plastic cover, blood-stained clothes, ornament and steel rod recoveries; homicidal death
evidence_type.quote: The High Court also mentioned two other circumstances, namely, that the deceased met with a homicidal death
evidence_type.reason: The judgment never states absence of medical or eyewitness proof; that part of the value is unsupported.

confession.reason: Voluntary disclosure leading to recoveries and the s.313 fingerprint answer are both supported.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: No aggravating facts are noted by the court.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted by the court.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court acquitted the accused, giving benefit of doubt; no sentence was imposed.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court set aside acquittal; judgment refers to the conviction arising from its decision.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court allowed the appeal and acquitted the accused.

offence_finally_established.reason: The accused is acquitted of murder and no offence stands established.

imprisonment_type.reason: No sentence is imposed after acquittal, so 'none' applies.

imprisonment_years.reason: No fixed-term sentence exists, so null is correct.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is imposed, so null is correct.

neutral_facts.reason: Roughly 280 words, uses 'the accused' and 'the victim', and omits court outcomes.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the prescribed punishment for s.302.

attempt_completion.reason: The victim was killed, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.reason: Death by homicide is the harm described.

number_of_offences.reason: Two charges (murder and theft), with none finally upheld after acquittal.

financial_property_loss.reason: Cash and ornaments valued at about Rs. 25,000 are noted, and the ornaments were not linked to the victim.

premeditation_planning.reason: The court made no finding of premeditation or planning.

motive.reason: Theft of ornaments is recorded as the alleged motive.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Presence at house around 1 p.m. treated as doubtful, not accepted; victim alive until about 8.30 p.m. with others present; steel rod recovery at accused's instance and homicidal death noted; fingerprint, blood-group and ornament evidence rejected
key_evidence_accepted.quote: There is a clear doubt whether the appellant was with the deceased
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Presence at 1 p.m. was not accepted as established; it was only treated as the best the evidence showed.

witness_credibility.reason: Fingerprint expert's bona fides, weak PW-6/PW-7 identification and inconsequential photographer evidence are all supported.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: High Court found absconding; Supreme Court did not specifically discuss it. Accused made a voluntary disclosure leading to ornament and steel rod recoveries; apprehended 11 Nov 1990 about 4.45 p.m.
post_offence_conduct.quote: Prakash made a voluntary disclosure to the Investigating Officer
post_offence_conduct.reason: Omits the disclosure, and the court did not specifically reject absconding as proof of guilt.

custody_duration.reason: The judgment does not state how long the accused was in custody.

bail_history.reason: No bail information appears in the judgment.

trial_duration.reason: All listed dates match the judgment, including the SC date in the header.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for appellant and respondent match the judgment's header.

investigation_status.reason: FIR registration, charge sheet and completed trial are supported.

procedural_irregularity.reason: Each listed lapse (no TIP, fingerprint issues, unexamined relative, s.313 omission) is noted by the court.

appeal_history.reason: Trial acquittal, High Court reversal and Supreme Court acquittal match the judgment.

prosecution_argument.reason: The judgment does not record the prosecution's arguments before the Supreme Court.

defence_argument.correct_value: Photographs did not show the plastic cover, so it was planted later; accused said fingerprint was taken on 7 Nov 1990; serologist report was not put to him
defence_argument.quote: the plastic cover was planted subsequently
defence_argument.reason: The ornament identification point is not recorded as a defence argument; it is the court's own discussion.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Certainty required in circumstantial cases, benefit of doubt, non-mandatory TIP and fingerprint fairness are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Relied on: Ravi Kapur; R. Shaji; Rameshwar Singh; Mulla v. State of U.P.; Kishore Chand; Boota Singh; Malkhan Singh; Visveswaran; Hanumant Govind Nargundkar; Narain Singh; Dadarao; Mohd. Aman; Tara Singh. Marcouix and Mezzo only referred to.
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Marcouix v. The Queen (1976) 1 SCR 763 Referred to Para 27
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Marcouix and Mezzo were only referred to, and Mulla, Kishore Chand and Boota Singh are omitted.

sentencing_rationale.reason: No sentence was imposed, so the rationale is not applicable.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The court weighed no mitigating factors.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The court weighed no aggravating factors.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or other orders are given.
